title: Cultivating clear seeing
opening: Before you share a draft, “This will fail” may come up. You can notice the thought and the effort to push it away, then inspect what the draft needs.

steps.label: Notice
steps.description: If you catch yourself trying to make the thought disappear or thinking “I'm doing this wrong,” include that effort in what you notice.

steps.label: Receive
steps.description: A sensation, perception, thought or emotion may already be here. Give it your attention without waiting to feel calmer or have a special insight.

steps.label: Observe
steps.description: A sensation may change, a thought may come and go, and a feeling may intensify or fade. The thought “This will fail” predicts the whole draft will fail. Inspect the example sentence before deciding whether that prediction fits.

steps.label: Return
steps.description: If “This will fail” feels less convincing, notice that. If it still feels convincing, do not force yourself to disbelieve it or replace it with reassurance. Check what the draft actually needs, then do what the situation calls for.

statements.text: “Every learner will understand this after one lesson.”
statements.feedback: This example sentence has no source. Check what supports the claim, then ask whether one unsupported sentence means the whole draft will fail.

ownPursuit.prompt: Choose a recent, ordinary moment in your pursuit that feels comfortable to think about.
ownPursuit.prediction: What did you tell yourself would happen, or what were you trying to make yourself think or feel?
ownPursuit.observation: What sensation, perception, thought or feeling did you notice at the time?
ownPursuit.revision: What does the situation call for now, whether or not the belief loosens?

accessibility.step: Four steps for noticing a thought and returning to what the situation calls for
accessibility.ownPursuit: Write and save a reflection about one thought, what you noticed and what the situation calls for
